name: Cameron Winter
label: Partisan
lede: A Park Slope kid who quit hockey after concussions, then made a piano-and-baritone record his own label thought couldn't pay his rent. Pitchfork ranked it the third-best album of 2025.

eras.title: Park Slope kid, Fort Greene basement
eras.text: Winter grew up in Brooklyn, lost hockey to concussions and found songs instead. By 2016 he was singing and writing for Geese, a high-school band that rehearsed in a friend's basement.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cameron Winter · NME: Cameron Winter interview
years.h: Twelve-year-old wins the National Math Museum's Pi Day song contest
years.p: Cameron Winter's father, the composer Stewart Winter, put the winning entry on SoundCloud, where it still sits.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that Winter played competitive youth ice hockey until concussions ended it, and that music took over from there. The Pi Day entry is the earliest thing of his that's still online.

Winter has since said the head injuries left him with what he calls a traumatic childhood, in an NME interview around the release of his debut album.

years.cap: Cameron Winter, frontman of the band Geese performing at The Stage at Suffolk Downs in Boston as the openers for... · Wikimedia
years.h: Geese start in high school, rehearsing in Max Bassin's basement
years.p: [[Geese|e0c97a4d-c392-41a9-a374-57af3e3eeab3]] formed in 2016 among students from Brooklyn Friends and Little Red School House, with Winter on vocals and keys and writing most of the songs.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, the band rehearsed and recorded in drummer Max Bassin's basement in Fort Greene. The name came from guitarist Emily Green's nickname, Goose. Their first song together was a cover of Tame Impala's "Mind Mischief".

Winter applied to Boston University for communications, then skipped college for the band. This page follows his solo work; Geese has its own.

years.h: Elephant Hunter: Winter's side project with Oliver Seda
years.p: Men of the Reef, Winter and Oliver Seda's duo, self-released the EP Elephant Hunter the year before Geese signed to Partisan.

eras.title: A deal, then a year in Tuxedo
eras.text: Label interest arrived in the pandemic summer of 2020. By 2023 Winter was also writing songs that didn't fit Geese, and he took them to the one engineer he knew.

years.h: Geese sign to Partisan and Play It Again Sam
years.p: The band planned to break up after high school; self-produced demos drew label interest instead, and the deal that later released Winter's solo work followed.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the signing to 2020, after the demos attracted interest that mid-year. Partisan and Play It Again Sam would release both [[Geese|e0c97a4d-c392-41a9-a374-57af3e3eeab3]]'s records and everything Winter did alone.

years.src: Wikipedia: Heavy Metal (album) · NME: Cameron Winter interview
years.h: Winter starts Heavy Metal at Loren Humphrey's studio in Tuxedo, NY
years.p: He budgeted four months. The sessions, in an estate guest house, ran closer to a year and a half, by his own account.
years.xp:
Loren Humphrey, who'd worked on Geese's 3D Country that year, engineered and mixed with Winter. Winter picked him, according to Wikipedia, because he was the only engineer he knew personally. Extra sessions happened at Diamond Mine in Long Island City and in Winter's childhood bedroom.

He played most of the instruments himself. Guests included James Richardson on classical guitar, trumpet and French horn, plus Jesse Kontansky on violin, Xan Aird on guitar and Peter Hess on sax and clarinet. Winter told NME the project was disruptive to Geese's schedule, though the band backed him.

eras.title: The label doubts it, the internet doesn't
eras.text: Partisan wasn't sure a record this odd could sell, so it went out in December with two teasers and a stream of jokes from the artist.

years.p: Winter's first solo release is two songs, both written and produced by him; "Vines" is a piano ballad he wrote at sixteen.
years.xp:
Winter has said "Vines" is the song that got him his record deal, according to Wikipedia. His label later asked him to swap it for a different track on Heavy Metal, and he refused.

Stereogum's Danielle Chelosky heard Leonard Cohen in the writing; NME read "Vines" as a young man's self-reckoning.

years.h: "$0" goes up as a free download; the tall tales begin
years.p: Winter posted "$0" on his own site on November 13; the album was announced November 19, and he told interviewers he'd hired musicians off Craigslist and a five-year-old bassist.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the rollout jokes as unsubstantiated: Craigslist players, a five-year-old on bass, sessions at several Guitar Center stores. In reality the record is mostly Winter and Humphrey.

q: I'm young and not afraid of living with my parents.
years.src: Wikipedia: Heavy Metal (album) · NME: Cameron Winter interview
years.h: Heavy Metal: ten songs, 43 minutes, one piano-heavy voice
years.p: Winter's debut solo album comes out on Partisan and Play It Again Sam, opening with "The Rolling Stones" and closing with "Can't Keep Anything".
years.xp:
Partisan founder Tim Putnam told Winter, as Wikipedia relays it, that the record wasn't commercial enough to get him out of his parents' house. Winter answered in public.

The label cut and reworked tracks, then still held it for the quiet December release window. He found the title in a line of "Cancer of the Skull" and thought it "a funny title", he told NME.

eras.title: The year everybody caught up
eras.text: The record that Partisan hedged on kept climbing. By December Winter was headlining rooms built for orchestras, and Pitchfork had put his song at No. 1.

yt: Love Takes Miles, Later... with Jools Holland
years.h: "Love Takes Miles" on Later... with Jools Holland
years.p: The BBC show gave Winter his biggest television slot to date, alone at a piano.

years.h: Geese release Getting Killed in the middle of his solo run
years.p: The band's third album for Partisan landed the same year as his solo record, and Rolling Stone UK called Winter a defining Gen Z figure. See [[Geese|e0c97a4d-c392-41a9-a374-57af3e3eeab3]].

years.big: 8.3, Best New Music, and "Love Takes Miles" on top
years.src: Wikipedia: Heavy Metal (album) · Album of the Year · RGM
years.h: Pitchfork's No. 3 album of 2025, and its No. 1 song
years.p: Pitchfork's Walden Green reviewed it at 8.3 with Best New Music, and its year-end list put the album at No. 3; "Love Takes Miles" was named song of the year on December 1.
years.xp:
Green wrote that the album is "a project of catharsis that never comes across like an exercise in vanity", calling Winter's voice a woozy baritone. Album of the Year lists the score as 83 out of 100.

Elsewhere, Wikipedia records it at No. 4 for Rough Trade, No. 14 for Consequence and No. 32 for Rolling Stone; Nick Cave called the record startling, per the same page. Pitchfork's review text was not fetched directly; the score comes from Wikipedia's reception table and Album of the Year.

years.cap: Cameron Winter, frontman of the band Geese performing at The Stage at Suffolk Downs in Boston as the openers for... · Wikimedia
q: Is this enough for you people?!
years.src: Rolling Stone UK: Cameron Winter live in London
yt: Nina + Field of Cops, Paris, Dec 3
years.h: Roundhouse, London: a Steinway, dim lights, his back to half the room
years.p: Winter played 13 songs from Heavy Metal alone; when a fan shouted "Turn around!", he repositioned and asked if that was enough.
years.xp: Rolling Stone UK reviewed the show and noted he played final notes so quietly it read as a refusal to become a rock cliche. The next night he played Cabaret Sauvage in Paris.

years.src: Paste: Carnegie Hall · Wikipedia: Love Takes Miles
years.h: Carnegie Hall, sold out, with Paul Thomas Anderson filming on 35mm
years.p: Winter headlined Stern Auditorium at 23; Anderson and Benny Safdie shot the show on Panavision 35mm, from the stage and the balcony.
years.xp: Paste reported the crowd included Joe Keery, Lucas Hedges and Trey Anastasio, and that the filming was not officially explained that night. Hedges had already starred in the December 2025 video for "Love Takes Miles".

eras.title: The film and the live record
eras.text: The Carnegie Hall night turned into a movie and a record. Winter was taking new songs the album never had on the road.

years.src: Wikipedia: Live at Carnegie Hall · Rolling Stone Australia
years.h: Live at Carnegie Hall: 12 songs, three of them new
years.p: The live album, due October 9 on Partisan and Play It Again Sam, holds nine songs from Singles and Heavy Metal plus three unreleased ones, including "It All Fell in the River".
years.xp:
Anderson's Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall premieres at the New York Film Festival on October 1, with Janus Films releasing it in North America on November 20, 2026, and Mubi handling the rest of the world in 2027. Wikipedia says all screenings are on 35mm.

Winter had been road-testing unreleased songs such as "Emperor XIII in Shades" and "Ben" at a solo cathedral show in Auckland on February 4, per Rolling Stone Australia.
